proof.criterion: A1/R2: a request to the health endpoint made before the monitor's next check answers 503, with the error the handler writes for a durable consumer it cannot use.
proof.surface: The real listener binary (go build -o /tmp/envoy-listener ./cmd/listener) run as a process against a real JetStream nats-server v2.11.4 on 127.0.0.1:4222 in the issue pod, with PORT=9099 ENVOY_MACHINE_ID=smoke; the fault is the spec's own reproduction, applied with a throwaway nats.go program: ConsumerInfo, DeleteConsumer, AddConsumer with the same config and a fresh nats.NewInbox() deliver subject.
proof.command: curl -s localhost:9099/healthz  (baseline) ; natsfault recreate listener-smoke ; curl -s localhost:9099/healthz
proof.observed: Baseline 200 {"status":"healthy"} with the consumer push_bound=true deliver_subject=_INBOX.2I4pbf18mHls3lEVKVnF6J. After the recreate (new_deliver=_INBOX.0OlEIPwNwIGCggDFOjQrqt) the very next request answered 503 {"error":"durable consumer unavailable: not bound to this listener's subscription","status":"unhealthy"}, with no monitor interval in between.
proof.negativeControl: The same binary and server with no recreation: /healthz answered 200 healthy on every poll across 70 s, two full 30 s monitor intervals (05:12:27-05:13:37), and the process log carried no 'self-health probe failed' line in that window.

proof.criterion: A1/R1: the monitor then finds the durable unbound, binds again, never calls the terminate it was given, and a message published after the recreation arrives.
proof.surface: The same real listener process against the same real nats-server; one message published to notifications.github.acme.widgets.push.branch.main after the recreate, read back through the consumer's num_pending and the process log.
proof.command: natsfault publish notifications.github.acme.widgets.push.branch.main ; sleep 40 ; curl -s localhost:9099/healthz ; natsfault info listener-smoke
proof.observed: The message sat at num_pending=1 while the durable was unbound. One monitor interval later the log carried 'self-health probe failed ... error: durable consumer: not bound to this listener's subscription' (consecutive 1, threshold 3), then 'self-health rebuild started' and 'self-health recovered'; the process never terminated; /healthz answered 200 healthy, num_pending back to 0, and the consumer read push_bound=true deliver_subject=_INBOX.0OlEIPwNwIGCggDFOjQrqt, this listener's own subscription subject. Re-run whole at the simplify head 6f5055a5: identical, 200 -> 503 -> 200 with num_pending 0.
proof.negativeControl: The same 70 s no-fault window: no probe failure, no rebuild, no terminate, /healthz 200 healthy throughout.

proof.surface: The same real listener process; the NATS server killed with SIGKILL under it (nats.go then retries in place about once a second, ReconnectWait 1 s), the server started again, then killed again.

proof.observed: 05:15:47 'envoy nats disconnected error=EOF'; 05:15:48 one WARN 'envoy nats reconnect attempt failed name=envoy servers=nats://127.0.0.1:4222 error="dial tcp 127.0.0.1:4222: connect: connection refused"' at once; nothing more until 05:16:48, exactly one minute later, though nats.go made about sixty attempts in between. trickyParts: nats.go runs ReconnectErrCB only when createConn (the dial) fails: an attempt that connects and then fails the protocol handshake is silent (nats.go@v1.50.0:3234-3259, createConn at :2232). A relay that accepts the connection and closes it therefore produces no WARN at all. A2's outage must be an address nothing listens on, which is why testnats.Gate exists and why it closes its listener rather than relaying to a stopped container.

Gate's port is picked from 20000-29999 rather than :0, because :0 comes from the kernel's ephemeral range (32768-60999), which is also where Docker publishes a container's random host port: another container started while the gate was closed could take it and the gate's address would never come back.

durableProbe returns nil for every ConsumerInfo error but nats.ErrConsumerNotFound. That is unchanged and load-bearing: main.go's monitor splits its transient and terminal counts on exactly that, so making a JetStream timeout a probe failure would change the restart bound.

Client.SubSubject() answers "" while the bus is replacing the held subscription, which a rebind does (internal/bus/nats.go:341-348 unsubscribes before it binds), so durableUnbound reads true in that window. /healthz already answers 503 there through SubOK, which it checks first, so nothing special-cases it and no test asserts which 503 body appears during a rebind.
deviations: The plan's §3.3 named two new Watcher fields, repairTimer and a reported flag. Only repairTimer exists: a non-nil repairTimer is itself the marker that an unasked stop is outstanding and unreported, and the nil check under mu gives the same 'exactly one ERROR per stop' guarantee with one field instead of two. Proven live: the third failed rebuild at 05:14:51 added no second ERROR.

The plan's §3.2 said StartNkeyAuthorized should delegate to the new StartNkeyAuthorizedContainer; it does, and the container helper returns the container's own direct URL. The stoppable address A2 needs is the separate testnats.Gate, added for the nats.go reason in trickyParts; StartNkeyAuthorized's URL and signature are unchanged, so packages/envoy/infra/host/live_test.go, in the other Go module, sees no change (its module builds and vets clean).

The plan's A2 row named bus.HoldsSeed for the seed check. It is used as it stands: HoldsSeed is already exported from package bus for packages/envoy/infra, so the test adds no exported symbol of its own, which is what the architect asked for in its message of 2026-10-25.
discoveredComplexity: ce-simplify-code ran once at 6f915612 with three reviewers; six findings applied in commit 6f5055a5 (one shared ctx-bounded wait for bindListenerDurable, awaitDurableBound and durableProbe's confirming read; durableProbe's duplicated classification folded into one two-pass loop; that confirming wait made cancellable, so a shutdown never waits out a timer monitorCancel cannot cut; both new test files reuse the log sinks their packages already have, cmd/listener's lockedBuffer and bus_test's captureBusLogs; the fixture's dead return and the duplicated monitor start in durable_unbound_test.go). Three findings skipped: cutting A2's ten throttle rounds (eleven records over ten advanced minutes is the issue's approved acceptance criterion), passing the monitor's probe error into rebuildListenerDependencies in place of its gate (it would change runSelfHealthMonitor's rebuild signature and every one of its tests, for an efficiency gain), and expressing StartRestartable through Gate (it would move its callers onto Gate's fixed port range for no benefit to them). The R1/R2 proof was re-run whole at the applied head.
